html:
Muziris was an ancient port on the Malabar coast of south India, near the mouth of the Periyar river in today's Kerala. It was the leading pepper port of the Chera kingdom and the main Indian goal of Roman ships sailing from Egypt.

Tamil Sangam poems describe the "beautiful large ships of the Yavanas", meaning Greeks and Romans, arriving with gold and leaving with pepper. Greek and Latin writers, from the Periplus to Pliny the Elder, name it. A papyrus from the 2nd century, the Muziris papyrus, records a loan for a cargo shipped from here to Alexandria, worth a fortune.

Its site was long lost; the river probably silted up, and a great flood in 1341 changed the coast. Since 2007, digs at Pattanam near Kodungallur have found Roman amphorae, glass and coins, beads and a brick wharf, and many scholars now see it as part of Muziris.

The pepper trade ran on through Arab and Chinese merchants, and later the Portuguese at Calicut up the same coast. It also linked the Tamil kingdoms to the wider Indian Ocean trade.
